library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Tomizawa_2017_cefmetazole"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Tomizawa_2017_cefmetazole"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1186/s40780-016-0071-6> (open access)

A literature check on 2026-11-25 (Europe PMC, the article's PMC record)
found no erratum or correction for this article, and the article has no
supplementary material.

# Population

Tomizawa 2017 studied 23 Japanese adults (18 men, 5 women; age 41-84
years, mean 69) who received cefmetazole as intraoperative antimicrobial
prophylaxis during elective surgery for colorectal cancer (colon 14,
rectum 9; laparoscopic 13, open 10) at Kitasato University Hospital
between November 2008 and December 2010 (Table 1). Body weight was
47.5-89.0 kg (mean 63.7) and Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance was
47.2-126.3 mL/min (mean 73.9). Cefmetazole 1 g was infused IV over 5-10
min after the induction of anaesthesia and within 60 min before incision,
then 1 g every 3 h; 86 serum concentrations were measured by HPLC.
Emergency surgery, ileus and dialysis were exclusions.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Tomizawa_2017_cefmetazole")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| One-compartment IV model (ADVAN1 TRANS2) | -- | Methods, Pharmacokinetics model |
| `cl = theta1 * CRCL` (no intercept) | -- | Table 3 'CLCMZ = theta1 x Ccr (L/h)'; Results text |
| `vc = theta2 * WT` (no intercept) | -- | Table 3 'VdCMZ = theta2 x BW (L)'; Results text |
| `lcl` | `log(0.0704)` L/h per mL/min | Table 3 theta1; Table 4 0.0704 +/- 0.0029 |
| `lvc` | `log(0.163)` L/kg | Table 3 theta2; Table 4 0.163 +/- 0.0054 |
| Exponential IIV `P_j = P x exp(eta_j)` | -- | Eq. 1 |
| `etalcl` | 0.0441 (= 0.210^2) | Table 3 omegaCL 21.0%; Table 4 omegaCL 0.210 |
| `etalvc` | 0.007056 (= 0.084^2) | Table 3 omegaVd 8.4%; Table 4 omegaVd 0.084 |
| Proportional residual `C = Cpred x (1 + eps)` | -- | Eq. 2 |
| `propSd` | 0.135 | Table 3 sigma 13.5%; Table 4 sigma 0.135 |
| Dose 1 g IV over 5-10 min, then 1 g every 3 h | -- | Methods, Data source |

# Typical-value check against the paper's own numbers

The Discussion states CL = 7.04 L/h at a creatinine clearance of 100
mL/min and a volume of 10.4 +/- 1.6 L across the cohort's 47.5-89.0 kg
body weights. The typical values from the packaged model reproduce both:
at the cohort mean weight (63.7 kg) V = 0.163 x 63.7 = 10.38 L.

```{r typical}
mod <- readModelDb("Tomizawa_2017_cefmetazole")
ini_df <- rxode2::rxode(mod)$iniDf
theta <- setNames(ini_df$est, ini_df$name)
cl_100 <- exp(theta[["lcl"]]) * 100
v_mean <- exp(theta[["lvc"]]) * 63.7
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Quantity = c("CL at CrCl 100 mL/min (L/h)", "V at 63.7 kg (L)"),
    Model = signif(c(cl_100, v_mean), 4),
    Paper = c("7.04 (Discussion)", "10.4 (Discussion, cohort mean)")
  )
)
stopifnot(
  abs(cl_100 / 7.04 - 1) < 1e-3,
  abs(v_mean / 10.4 - 1) < 0.01
)
```

# Virtual cohort and simulation of the study regimen

The virtual cohort draws body weight and creatinine clearance from
normal distributions with the Table 1 means and SDs, redrawing any value
outside the observed range (a range is a definition, not a clamp). Each
subject receives the study regimen: 1 g over 7.5 min at time 0 (after
induction) and 1 g every 3 h, for three doses in total (Figure 1 shows
up to three doses).

```{r cohort}
rtrunc_norm <- function(n, mean, sd, lo, hi) {
  out <- numeric(0)
  while (length(out) < n) {
    x <- rnorm(2 * n, mean, sd)
    out <- c(out, x[x >= lo & x <= hi])
  }
  out[seq_len(n)]
}

set.seed(20170101)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20170101)
n_sub <- 200
cohort <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  WT = rtrunc_norm(n_sub, 63.7, 9.9, 47.5, 89.0),
  CRCL = rtrunc_norm(n_sub, 73.9, 21.7, 47.2, 126.3)
)

obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 9, by = 0.1), 3 - 1e-3, 6 - 1e-3)))
dose_rows <- data.frame(
  time = c(0, 3, 6), amt = 1000, rate = 1000 / (7.5 / 60),
  evid = 1, cmt = "central"
)
obs_rows <- data.frame(
  time = obs_times, amt = NA_real_, rate = NA_real_,
  evid = 0, cmt = "central"
)
events <- tidyr::crossing(cohort, bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows)) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = c("WT", "CRCL")) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r vpc, fig.cap = "Simulated serum cefmetazole (median and 5th-95th percentiles, 200 virtual patients) under the study regimen of 1 g every 3 h. Compare with Figure 1 of Tomizawa 2017, which plots the observed concentrations against time after incision (dosing preceded incision by up to 60 min)."}
vpc <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), p50 = median(Cc), p95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
ggplot(vpc, aes(time, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after first dose (h)",
    y = "Serum cefmetazole (ug/mL)"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r vpc-check}
vpc_peak <- vpc[which.min(abs(vpc$time - 0.2)), ]
vpc_trough <- vpc[which.min(abs(vpc$time - (3 - 1e-3))), ]
# Figure 1 first-dose observations: about 80-145 ug/mL in the first hour
# after incision and 10-45 ug/mL at 2-3.5 h. Assert on the simulated
# median only (robust to which subjects land in the tails).
stopifnot(
  vpc_peak$p50 > 70, vpc_peak$p50 < 130,
  vpc_trough$p50 > 10, vpc_trough$p50 < 45
)
```

Just after the first infusion (0.2 h) the simulated median is
`r round(vpc_peak$p50)` ug/mL (5th-95th percentile
`r round(vpc_peak$p05)`-`r round(vpc_peak$p95)`), and just before the
second dose at 3 h it is `r round(vpc_trough$p50)` ug/mL
(`r round(vpc_trough$p05)`-`r round(vpc_trough$p95)`). Both sit in the
range of the first-dose observations in Figure 1 (about 80-145 ug/mL
early, 10-45 ug/mL at 2-3.5 h after incision).

# Replicate Table 5 (MIC target attainment)

Table 5 gives the percentage of simulated patients whose serum
cefmetazole stayed above the MIC80 of *Bacteroides fragilis* 2-6 h after
a single 1 g dose, by body-weight band and creatinine-clearance band
(Monte Carlo, 1000 replicates, run in Excel). The paper does not print
the MIC80 value or how weight and creatinine clearance were drawn inside
each band. The maintainers took the draws as uniform within each band,
treated the dose as a bolus, and back-solved the MIC from the table:
16 ug/mL reproduces all 45 cells (lattice check below), whereas 12 and 20 ug/mL
are far worse. The simulation below uses the packaged model's
between-subject variability (`Cc`, without residual error).

```{r table5-published}
table5 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~wt_band, ~crcl_band, ~`2`, ~`3`, ~`4`, ~`5`, ~`6`,
  "40-50", "90-130", 52.87, 3.39, 0.00, 0.00, 0.00,
  "40-50", "50-90", 91.24, 57.89, 19.42, 3.45, 0.37,
  "40-50", "10-50", 98.66, 96.67, 92.96, 81.20, 66.08,
  "50-60", "90-130", 72.44, 8.56, 0.14, 0.00, 0.00,
  "50-60", "50-90", 92.17, 72.40, 33.66, 8.28, 2.33,
  "50-60", "10-50", 98.19, 96.71, 93.43, 88.53, 74.18,
  "60-70", "90-130", 82.16, 15.57, 1.58, 0.00, 0.00,
  "60-70", "50-90", 92.69, 81.51, 44.25, 15.74, 4.78,
  "60-70", "10-50", 97.27, 96.06, 93.16, 90.56, 79.45
) |>
  pivot_longer(`2`:`6`, names_to = "time", values_to = "paper_pct") |>
  mutate(time = as.numeric(time))
band_lo <- function(x) as.numeric(sub("-.*", "", x))
band_hi <- function(x) as.numeric(sub(".*-", "", x))
cells <- distinct(table5, wt_band, crcl_band)
```

```{r table5-sim}
mic <- 16
n_cell <- 200
rxode2::rxSetSeed(5219696)
set.seed(5219696)
mc_cohort <- cells |>
  mutate(cell = row_number()) |>
  slice(rep(seq_len(n()), each = n_cell)) |>
  mutate(
    id = row_number(),
    WT = runif(n(), band_lo(wt_band), band_hi(wt_band)),
    CRCL = runif(n(), band_lo(crcl_band), band_hi(crcl_band))
  )
mc_events <- bind_rows(
  mc_cohort |> mutate(time = 0, amt = 1000, evid = 1),
  tidyr::crossing(mc_cohort, time = c(2, 3, 4, 5, 6)) |>
    mutate(amt = NA_real_, evid = 0)
) |>
  mutate(cmt = "central") |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
mc_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = mc_events,
  keep = c("wt_band", "crcl_band")
) |>
  as.data.frame()
pta <- mc_sim |>
  group_by(wt_band, crcl_band, time) |>
  summarise(sim_pct = 100 * mean(Cc > mic), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(table5, by = c("wt_band", "crcl_band", "time")) |>
  mutate(diff = sim_pct - paper_pct)

pta |>
  mutate(
    cell = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", sim_pct, paper_pct),
    time = paste0(time, " h")
  ) |>
  select(wt_band, crcl_band, time, cell) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = time, values_from = cell) |>
  rename(
    "Weight (kg)" = wt_band,
    "CrCl (mL/min)" = crcl_band
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    caption = "Percentage above MIC 16 ug/mL: simulated (Tomizawa 2017 Table 5)."
  )

# 200 subjects per cell gives a binomial SE of at most 3.5 percentage
# points. The largest gap between the model and the table on a 40000-point
# eta/covariate lattice is about 7 points (the 2-h cells near 92%, which the
# paper's Excel run puts lower than the model), so the envelope bound of 12
# sits above model error + 1.5 SE; the median gap is about 2.
stopifnot(
  median(abs(pta$diff)) < 5,
  quantile(abs(pta$diff), 0.9) < 12
)
```

## Variability scale and MIC, settled by Table 5

Table 3 prints the variabilities as CV% and Table 4 prints them as 0.210,
0.084 and 0.135. The packaged model reads these as standard deviations
of eta (variance = 0.210^2). The alternative reading, that 0.210 is
itself the variance, more than doubles the SD of log-clearance
(0.458 instead of 0.210). A deterministic
lattice over eta and the within-band covariates (no random numbers)
shows that only the standard-deviation reading reproduces Table 5, and
that the minimum lies at an MIC of 16 ug/mL.

```{r omega-scale}
lattice_pta <- function(sd_cl, sd_v, mic) {
  z_cl <- qnorm((seq_len(40) - 0.5) / 40)
  z_v <- qnorm((seq_len(10) - 0.5) / 10)
  u <- (seq_len(10) - 0.5) / 10
  grid <- expand.grid(z_cl = z_cl, z_v = z_v, u_wt = u, u_cr = u)
  res <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(cells)), function(i) {
    wt <- band_lo(cells$wt_band[i]) + 10 * grid$u_wt
    cr <- band_lo(cells$crcl_band[i]) +
      (band_hi(cells$crcl_band[i]) - band_lo(cells$crcl_band[i])) * grid$u_cr
    cl <- 0.0704 * cr * exp(sd_cl * grid$z_cl)
    v <- 0.163 * wt * exp(sd_v * grid$z_v)
    data.frame(
      wt_band = cells$wt_band[i], crcl_band = cells$crcl_band[i],
      time = 2:6,
      lat_pct = sapply(2:6, function(t) 100 * mean(1000 / v * exp(-cl / v * t) > mic))
    )
  })
  bind_rows(res) |>
    left_join(table5, by = c("wt_band", "crcl_band", "time"))
}
scan <- tidyr::crossing(
  reading = c("SD (packaged)", "variance"),
  mic = c(8, 12, 16, 20, 24)
) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    rms = {
      sds <- if (reading == "variance") sqrt(c(0.210, 0.084)) else c(0.210, 0.084)
      lp <- lattice_pta(sds[1], sds[2], mic)
      sqrt(mean((lp$lat_pct - lp$paper_pct)^2))
    }
  ) |>
  ungroup()
scan |>
  mutate(rms = round(rms, 1)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = mic, values_from = rms) |>
  rename("Omega reading" = reading) |>
  knitr::kable(
    caption = "RMS difference (percentage points) from Table 5 over 45 cells, by MIC (ug/mL)."
  )

best <- scan[which.min(scan$rms), ]
var_best <- min(scan$rms[scan$reading == "variance"])
stopifnot(
  best$reading == "SD (packaged)",
  best$mic == 16,
  best$rms < 4,
  var_best > 2 * best$rms
)
```

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports no NCA. The check below runs PKNCA on typical-value
single-dose profiles (1 g over 7.5 min) at the cohort mean weight and at
creatinine clearances of 50, 73.9 (cohort mean) and 100 mL/min, and
compares against the closed-form one-compartment values implied by the
Table 3 estimates: CL = 0.0704 x CrCl, V = 0.163 x 63.7,
AUC0-inf = 1000 / CL and t1/2 = ln 2 x V / CL.

```{r pknca}
nca_groups <- data.frame(
  id = 1:3,
  treatment = c("CrCl 50", "CrCl 73.9", "CrCl 100"),
  CRCL = c(50, 73.9, 100),
  WT = 63.7
)
nca_events <- bind_rows(
  nca_groups |> mutate(time = 0, amt = 1000, rate = 1000 / (7.5 / 60), evid = 1),
  tidyr::crossing(nca_groups, time = c(0, seq(0.05, 0.5, by = 0.05), seq(0.75, 24, by = 0.25))) |>
    mutate(amt = NA_real_, rate = NA_real_, evid = 0)
) |>
  mutate(cmt = "central") |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
# Three typical-value subjects; rxode2 warns that a multi-subject solve
# has no omega, which is the intent of zeroRe().
nca_sim <- suppressWarnings(rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod),
  events = nca_events,
  keep = "treatment"
)) |>
  as.data.frame()

conc_df <- nca_sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, treatment, time, Cc)
dose_df <- nca_events |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, treatment, time, amt)
conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | treatment + id, concu = "mg/L", timeu = "h")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id, doseu = "mg")
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

reference <- nca_groups |>
  mutate(
    cl = 0.0704 * CRCL,
    v = 0.163 * WT,
    aucinf.obs = 1000 / cl,
    half.life = log(2) * v / cl
  ) |>
  select(treatment, aucinf.obs, half.life)

tbl <- ncaComparisonTable(
  nca_res, reference,
  by = "treatment",
  params = c("aucinf.obs", "half.life"),
  units = c(aucinf.obs = "mg*h/L", half.life = "h")
)
knitr::kable(tbl, caption = "Simulated (PKNCA) vs closed form from Table 3.")

nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
  select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  left_join(reference, by = "treatment", suffix = c("_sim", "_ref"))
stopifnot(
  all(abs(nca_wide$aucinf.obs_sim / nca_wide$aucinf.obs_ref - 1) < 0.01),
  all(abs(nca_wide$half.life_sim / nca_wide$half.life_ref - 1) < 0.01)
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Through-origin covariate models.** Table 2 screened clearance as
  `theta1 + theta2 x Ccr` and volume as `theta1 + theta2 x BW`, but the
  final model (Table 3, Results text, abstract) is `CL = theta1 x Ccr`
  and `Vd = theta2 x BW` with no intercept. The packaged model follows
  the final model.
- **Creatinine clearance is raw Cockcroft-Gault mL/min.** The paper
  states the Cockcroft-Gault equation but not which body weight it used;
  total body weight is assumed. Values are not normalized to 1.73 m^2.
- **Variability scale.** The Table 4 omegas (0.210, 0.084) are taken as
  standard deviations of eta, so the variances are 0.0441 and 0.007056;
  this is the reading that reproduces Table 5 (see above). The residual
  error 0.135 is the SD of the proportional epsilon in Eq. 2.
- **Table 5 inputs not printed by the paper.** The MIC80 of
  *B. fragilis* (16 ug/mL) was back-solved by the maintainers from
  Table 5; the paper cites a 2004 Japanese surveillance report that is
  not in its reference list. Weight and creatinine clearance were drawn
  uniformly within each band and the dose was treated as a bolus.
  Table 5 lists weight bands up to 70 kg only.
- **Infusion duration.** The study infused each 1 g dose over 5-10 min;
  simulations here use 7.5 min.
- **Race.** Not tabulated; the single-centre Japanese cohort is recorded
  as Japanese.
- Only one patient had a creatinine clearance below 50 mL/min, so the
  model is weakly informed below that range (Discussion).
